open_points.subject: A28 wall-clock read cardinality
open_points.text: “the wall clock gives the instant: ... one reading per request” contradicts “An operation reads the clock once for its own timestamps” and “the audit writer: the writer takes it when it appends.”
open_points.question: Does one HTTP request receive one shared wall instant, or may each operation in that request—including the audit writer—call system_clock.utc_now separately?
options: One wall reading shared by every operation and audit append in the request
One wall reading per operation, with a separate audit-writer reading
One wall reading per use-case operation, but the audit receives the use-case instant
open_points.default_guess: Use one reading per operation and a separate audit-writer reading, preserving the explicit audit exception.

witness.initial: An active staff account submits valid credentials and the wall clock advances between session creation and audit append.
events: staff_identity.authenticate_staff creates a session and needs created_at/expires_at
outcomes: Both records use the single request instant because A28 permits one wall reading per request
The session uses authenticate_staff's instant and the audit uses append_audit's later instant because A28 assigns readings per operation and explicitly gives the writer its own reading
witness.observer: An administrator or test reading the persisted session and audit timestamps

open_points.subject: State 4 flows that require the current wall instant
open_points.text: “Only system_clock reads the host clocks ... An operation that needs the current instant takes one wall reading from it and reuses it,” but no State 4 flow names capability:system_clock.utc_now, its caller, or its position in the operation.
open_points.question: For each time-consuming operation in audit_writer, authorization_guard, staff_identity, staff_bootstrap, viewer_access, service_identity, snapshot_import, budget_management, expense_intake, expense_management, project_tracking and photo_management, where does the owning operation call utc_now relative to validation, expiry checks, repository reads and writes?
options: Each owning operation calls utc_now at entry and reuses it
Each owning operation calls utc_now after validation but before its first time comparison or timestamp construction
A route or outer caller reads utc_now and passes the instant into the owning operation
open_points.default_guess: Have each owning operation call utc_now immediately before its first current-time comparison or construction of portal-owned timestamps and reuse that instant.

witness.initial: A valid viewer credential exists and expires or is revoked while an entry request is being processed; the clock crosses a relevant boundary between validation and persistence.
events: viewer_access validates the credential and creates a ViewerSession with created_at and expires_at
outcomes: viewer_access reads utc_now before validation, so the credential is evaluated at the earlier instant and the session timestamps derive from it
viewer_access reads utc_now after validation, so the same request is refused or receives later session timestamps
witness.observer: The viewer, and a persistence test inspecting whether a session was created and its timestamps

open_points.subject: Viewer-entry elapsed-clock step
open_points.text: “the transport guard takes the elapsed reading for the viewer-entry window from it,” while flow:viewer_entry_and_session only says “module:transport_guard has already rate-limited entry per client address” and never names capability:system_clock.monotonic_seconds.
open_points.question: When and by whom is monotonic_seconds called in the transport-guard sequence, including whether non-entry requests call it and whether the reading occurs before bucket lookup, eviction, limit testing or bucket update?
options: transport_guard calls monotonic_seconds only for viewer-entry requests, before all bucket work
transport_guard calls it once for every request and uses it only for viewer-entry requests
transport_guard calls it for viewer entry after locating or evicting buckets but before testing and updating the selected bucket
open_points.default_guess: Call monotonic_seconds once only for a viewer-entry request, immediately before rate-limit bucket processing.

witness.initial: A client-address bucket is at the limit and its oldest attempt is exactly at the window boundary.
events: The client sends another viewer-entry request
transport_guard canonicalizes the route, obtains elapsed time, expires or retains old bucket entries, tests the limit and possibly calls viewer_access
outcomes: The elapsed reading is taken before bucket processing; the oldest entry falls outside the window and verification proceeds
The reading is taken later or bucket expiry is evaluated using another moment; the oldest entry remains and the request is refused before verification
witness.observer: The viewer receiving either the normal entry result or the concealed rate-limit refusal
